name: Yuki Konohana
equipment: A carved fox-charm netsuke (omamori of the kitsune)
A costume of bright travelling-player's silks
A book of songs, riddles, and old folktales
features: Fey Ancestry (advantage on saves against being charmed; magic can't put you to sleep)
Bardic Inspiration (bonus action to grant an ally a d6 to add to an ability check, attack, or save; uses equal to Charisma modifier per long rest)
Spellcasting (Charisma-based arcane magic woven through music)
Ritual Casting (cast known bard spells with the ritual tag without expending a slot)
By Popular Demand (Entertainer feature: welcome and free lodging wherever you perform)

personality.traits: I never met a stranger I couldn't tease into a smile, and I tell every story a little better than it happened. 🦊 I trail a faint scent of autumn leaves and trouble. When the mood turns heavy, I will be the one cracking a joke from the back of the room.
personality.ideals: Freedom. The road belongs to those who walk it, and a song sung in chains is no song at all. I tug at the strings of stuffy lords and grasping priests because someone ought to, and because it is delightful.
personality.bonds: My grandmother was a kitsune, a fox-spirit who fell in love with a wandering musician — my grandfather — and her blood runs warm and mischievous in me. The fox-charm I carry was hers, and I am following old family stories back toward the spirit-shrine she came from.
personality.flaws: I cannot resist a clever lie or a beautiful face, and my tongue has written cheques my blade cannot cash. I run from anything that feels too much like staying — including, sometimes, people who deserve better.

appearance: A striking, quick-smiling wanderer of Hinomoto with a fey-tinged beauty that draws second glances. ⛩️ Their eyes are a warm amber-gold that catch the light strangely, and at the corners of a grin there's something just a touch too sharp — fox-spirit blood, the old folk whisper. Russet-black hair falls loose past their shoulders, and they dress in travelling-player's silks of persimmon orange and deep red, a carved fox-mask pushed up onto their brow. A shamisen rides across their back and a bamboo flute at their hip, and a small fox-charm netsuke hangs from their sash. They move with a dancer's looseness, always half a step from a bow, a wink, or a vanishing trick.
backstory: Yuki Konohana is the grandchild of a kitsune — one of the shapeshifting fox-spirits of the old tales — who, the family story goes, took human form for the love of a wandering shamisen player and bore him a half-spirit child. That fox-blood thinned over the generations but never quite faded, surfacing in Yuki as uncanny charm, amber eyes that gleam in the dark, and a mischief that no scolding ever cured. Orphaned young and raised by a troupe of travelling entertainers, Yuki learned the shamisen and the flute, the arts of song, sleight-of-hand, and the kind of honeyed talk that opens purses and palace doors alike. They became a roving performer in the floating world — playing for peasants at festival fires one week and gulling a fat magistrate out of his rice-tax the next, always laughing, always moving on before the trouble caught up. Lately, though, the old fox-charm their grandmother left has begun to feel warm against their skin near certain shrines, and dreams of a moonlit fox-spirit grove have grown insistent. So Yuki travels with a purpose now, beneath all the songs and grinning misdirection: to follow their grandmother's spirit-blood back to its source, and to learn at last what the fox in their veins truly wants of them.
